headline: City agree record Fernandez fee; Arsenal's Alvarez picture unclear
paragraphs: Manchester City have agreed a British transfer-record £125m deal to sign Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez, reported independently by BBC Sport, Sky Sports, the Guardian and Transfermarkt — the best-corroborated story in today's feed. None of the four describe an official club announcement; all describe an agreed fee, not a completed signing. Sky's Jamie Carragher argued the move makes City, not any other side, the leading challenger to Arsenal's title defense.

Arsenal's form on the pitch is settled: Bukayo Saka's goal beat Aston Villa 1-0, reported by both the Guardian and Opta Analyst, extending an unbeaten start to two league wins, though FourFourTwo says Declan Rice limped off with a possible injury, unconfirmed. Off the pitch, reports conflict over Julian Álvarez — BBC's gossip column has Arsenal still pursuing the forward, while Sky Sports notes he was training with Atlético on deadline day and Transfermarkt's live blog asked whether he simply stays there. Nothing is resolved.

Liverpool's business was smaller: BBC Sport confirms winger Harvey Elliott has joined Valencia on a season-long loan, while a separate BBC gossip roundup says the club rejected a £30m Nottingham Forest bid for Trey Nyoni. FourFourTwo reports, unconfirmed, that Liverpool will finish the window without a new central midfielder and are weighing a Stuttgart forward as a Mohamed Salah alternative. Real Madrid's only mention: BBC Sport says Fulham have agreed to sign the fringe midfielder Manuel Angel from them. No Bayern or PSG news ran today.
drop: Goodwin leaves hospital but still absent from Dundee Utd role
